clue.text: Accomplished players under a cloud

parts.note: something accomplished is finished or done with, i.e. over
the actors in a play make up its cast

explanation.surface: A troupe of skilled actors has fallen into disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under a cloud' reads as being in disgrace, but here it is literal: a sky under cloud cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky that is overcast is completely covered by grey cloud.

clue.text: Mollusc dear to Dodie Smith

explanation.surface: A shellfish beloved of a British playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodie Smith, author of The Hundred and One Dalmatians, also wrote the 1938 play Dear Octopus, its title a figure for the family's clinging grip.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-armed cephalopod is a mollusc, and Dodie Smith's play is titled Dear Octopus, so the creature is literally 'dear' to her.

clue.text: They teach English soldiers about foreign money

indicators.note: the English soldiers are wrapped about the coin, so the coin sits inside them

parts.note: ORS stands for other ranks, i.e. ordinary soldiers
a ducat is an old gold coin used across continental Europe

explanation.surface: Instructors tell English troops about overseas currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The ducat goes between E and ORS, so 'about' spreads the English soldiers around the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers and tutors are people whose job is to educate.

clue.text: Character actor initially getting laughs in the company

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the words Character and actor

parts.note: hoots are loud bursts of laughter

explanation.surface: A character actor gets laughs from the rest of the theatre troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In cahoots' means in partnership, so the word itself means company or alliance; 'in' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cahoots is a partnership or collusion, a joint company of people working together.

clue.text: Race cars that don't require a crank are not so common

indicators.note: to crank is to turn or wind, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: the letter given as written, which the cars no longer need

explanation.surface: Racing cars that start without a crank handle are rarer.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of RACE CARS, less the A that they 'don't require', are cranked into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarcer is rarer, comparatively harder to find.

clue.text: White porcelain is extracted from a French capitalist

indicators.note: the word is is pulled out of the inhabitant of the capital

parts.note: an inhabitant of the French capital is a Parisian; capitalist is read as one who lives in the capital
taken as written

explanation.surface: Porcelain is taken off a wealthy French businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitalist' suggests a financier, but it means a citizen of a capital city, here Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Parian ware is an unglazed white biscuit porcelain imitating marble from the island of Paros.

clue.text: Some crest for a bird!

parts.note: some means a part of something
a crest is the top line of a hill, a ridge

explanation.surface: A bit of plumage on a bird's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird's crest is a red herring: the crest is a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey partridge is a plump game bird.

clue.text: Note purchase of a repeated item

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
purchase in the sense of leverage or grip, a prise

explanation.surface: A note records buying the same item twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' means a firm grip or leverage, not a buy.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repeated passage or performance, as of a song returning later in a show.

clue.text: Sailor with brains, say, but no presence

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: say signals that the word for brains is spoken, and its sound written down

parts.note: brains here means good sense or intelligence

explanation.surface: A clever sailor nonetheless lacks any charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presence' looks like charisma; read it as being present, so its lack is being away.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence is the state of being away, the opposite of being present.

clue.text: Prepare for an early retirement when this is lit

definitions.text: Prepare for an early retirement when this is lit

parts.words: Prepare for an early retirement when this is lit
parts.note: fireworks carry the instruction to light the fuse paper and retire immediately; the 'retirement' is stepping back, not leaving work

explanation.surface: Something whose lighting signals it is time to quit work early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early retirement' suggests leaving a job; on a firework packet, 'retire' means stand well back.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the slow-burning fuse paper on a firework, after lighting which one retires to a safe distance.

clue.text: A little drink knocked back in Italy

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, here read as the letters turned round

parts.note: a sip is a small mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: Someone downs a small drink while holidaying in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' means gulped down in the surface but reversal in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan city famous for its leaning tower lies in Italy.

clue.text: One or two musical instruments

parts.note: a single bellows-driven instrument whose name joins the names of two separate instruments, a keyboard and a squeeze-box

explanation.surface: A vague reference to a few instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is one instrument, yet it is also the names of two instruments side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a single keyboard squeeze-box, but its name strings together a keyboard instrument and a free-reed instrument.

clue.text: Witness who makes promises for a small charge

definitions.text: who makes promises for a small charge

explanation.surface: A witness who takes small fees for making pledges.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'small charge' sounds like a fee; it is a child in someone's care, for whom a godparent makes baptismal vows.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent at baptism stands witness and makes vows on behalf of the infant, a little person in their care.

clue.text: Umpire's call, the crowd said, was "caught by accident"

parts.note: in cricket the umpire calls 'over' after six balls

indicators.note: said signals that the word for a crowd is spoken, and its sound written down

parts.note: a herd is a crowd, especially of animals or people

explanation.surface: At a cricket match the umpire's decision is heard by the crowd as 'caught'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like a cricket dismissal; here it means heard. In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Words overheard are picked up unintentionally by someone who was not meant to hear them.

clue.text: Stuck present in supplement

indicators.note: in places the word for present within the word for supplement

parts.note: to supplement is to add
someone present is here

explanation.surface: A gift is glued inside a magazine supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' reads as a gift but means being here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that adhered clung or became fixed to a surface.

clue.text: Topless assistant in ceremony has to be concealed

indicators.note: in puts the trimmed assistant inside the word for a ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a ceremonial act

indicators.note: topless means the assistant loses its first letter

parts.note: a second is an assistant, as to a duellist or boxer

explanation.surface: A topless helper at a ritual has to be kept out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' reads as nudity at a ritual, but it only beheads the helper, a duellist's second.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite knowledge is obscure, hidden from ordinary understanding.

clue.text: Get rid of money that's the source of resentment.

parts.note: cash is money
i.e., Latin id est, means that is

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, here of resentment

explanation.surface: Throwing away money because it breeds bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: To cashier is to dismiss someone, especially an officer, from service.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss them from the armed forces in disgrace.

clue.text: The sound of letters being put down means it's morning

definitions.text: The sound of letters being put down means it's morning

parts.words: The sound of letters being put down means it's morning
parts.note: in old signallers' spelling alphabet the two letters of the abbreviation for before noon were spoken as words, so writing them down means morning

explanation.surface: Hearing the post land on the mat tells you it is morning.
explanation.walkthrough: British army signallers in the First World War spoke A as 'ack' and M as 'emma', so A.M. was said this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Signallers' spoken form of a.m., the abbreviation for the hours before noon.

clue.text: Decay of tooth quickly apparent

indicators.note: decay breaks something down, so the letters fall apart and recombine

explanation.surface: Tooth decay shows up fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparent' is a link: the answer is apparent from the decay of OF TOOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To go hotfoot is to go in great haste.

clue.text: Broadcast in place for water fowl

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio report on a waterbird in its habitat.
explanation.definitionFit: The large-billed seabird with a throat pouch is a water bird.

clue.text: Musician put up cup in Channel Islands for composition

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word cup is written upwards
composition here means making up anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician hoisted a trophy in Jersey for his new piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' suits a down clue, where reversing means writing upwards; 'composition' doubles as the opera the surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Puccini was the Italian opera composer of La Bohème and Tosca.

clue.text: Clumsy fellows are cry-babies when bowled out

indicators.note: out says the letter for bowled is removed

parts.note: blubbers are people who weep noisily
b is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: Awkward men are crybabies when dismissed at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled out' suggests a cricket dismissal; it means take away B.
explanation.definitionFit: Lubbers are big, awkward, clumsy people, as in landlubber.

clue.text: Recorded music using sound of cymbals

definitions.text: Recorded music using sound of cymbals

parts.words: Recorded music using sound of cymbals
parts.note: music written down is set out in written signs, and cymbals sounds like a word for such signs

explanation.surface: A recording made with clashing percussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorded' suggests audio, and 'cymbals' sounds like 'symbols': music written in symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Music that has been notated is written down in musical notation, a system of symbols.

clue.text: Unofficial political advisers — some crocks here, probably

explanation.surface: A leader's informal circle of advisers is full of old crocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crocks' are old crockery stored in a cupboard, but also a jibe at worn-out old advisers.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader's informal circle of advisers, and also a cupboard where crockery is kept.

clue.text: Short shot in a medal round

parts.note: MM is the Military Medal
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A brief gunshot fired during a medal ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' signals the abbreviated word: the answer is short for ammunition, which is shot.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a clipped form of ammunition, the shot and bullets fired from guns.

clue.text: Vigorous heel from those who are fit for the fray

definitions.text: those who are fit for the fray

parts.note: vigorous means energetic, active
a ship that heels over lists to one side

explanation.surface: An energetic cad emerging from among those fit to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heel' means a cad in the surface but is the nautical verb to lean.
explanation.definitionFit: The roll of officers available for full military service, those fit to serve.

clue.text: Persecuted for a debit, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of a debit could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Hounded over a debit on one's account.
explanation.definitionFit: To bait someone is to torment or harass them, as dogs once tormented bears.

clue.text: How fast one is flying, bearing drug

parts.note: air means bearing or manner, as in an air of confidence
speed is slang for amphetamine

explanation.surface: Questioning an airline pilot's velocity while carrying narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like a compass direction but means demeanour.
explanation.definitionFit: The speed of an aircraft relative to the surrounding air.
